units.leftText: The revelation which Habakkuk the prophet saw.
units.rightText: The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see.

units.leftText: LORD, how long will I cry, and you will not hear? I cry out to you “Violence!” and will you not save?
units.rightText: O Jehovah, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear? I cry out unto thee of violence, and thou wilt not save.
leftNotes: 1:2 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: Why do you show me iniquity, and look at perversity? For destruction and violence are before me. There is strife, and contention rises up.
units.rightText: Why dost thou show me iniquity, and look upon perverseness? for destruction and violence are before me; and there is strife, and contention riseth up.

units.leftText: Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails; for the wicked surround the righteous; therefore justice comes out perverted.
units.rightText: Therefore the law is slacked, and justice doth never go forth; for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore justice goeth forth perverted.

units.leftText: “Look among the nations, watch, and wonder marvelously; for I am working a work in your days which you will not believe though it is told you.
units.rightText: Behold ye among the nations, and look, and wonder marvellously; for I am working a work in your days, which ye will not believe though it be told you.

units.leftText: For, behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation who march through the width of the earth, to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.
units.rightText: For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, that march through the breadth of the earth, to possess dwelling-places that are not theirs.
leftNotes: 1:6 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: They are feared and dreaded. Their judgment and their dignity proceed from themselves.
units.rightText: They are terrible and dreadful; their judgment and their dignity proceed from themselves.

units.leftText: Their horses also are swifter than leopards, and are more fierce than the evening wolves. Their horsemen press proudly on. Yes, their horsemen come from afar. They fly as an eagle that hurries to devour.
units.rightText: Their horses also are swifter than leopards, and are more fierce than the evening wolves; and their horsemen press proudly on: yea, their horsemen come from far; they fly as an eagle that hasteth to devour.

units.leftText: All of them come for violence. Their hordes face forward. They gather prisoners like sand.
units.rightText: They come all of them for violence; the set of their faces is forwards; and they gather captives as the sand.

units.leftText: Yes, they scoff at kings, and princes are a derision to them. They laugh at every stronghold, for they build up an earthen ramp and take it.
units.rightText: Yea, he scoffeth at kings, and princes are a derision unto him; he derideth every stronghold; for he heapeth up dust, and taketh it.

units.leftText: Then they sweep by like the wind and go on. They are indeed guilty, whose strength is their god.”
units.rightText: Then shall he sweep by as a wind, and shall pass over, and be guilty, even he whose might is his god.

units.leftText: Aren’t you from everlasting, LORD my God, my Holy One? We will not die. LORD, you have appointed them for judgment. You, Rock, have established him to punish.
units.rightText: Art not thou from everlasting, O Jehovah my God, my Holy One? we shall not die. O Jehovah, thou hast ordained him for judgment; and thou, O Rock, hast established him for correction.

units.leftText: You who have purer eyes than to see evil, and who cannot look on perversity, why do you tolerate those who deal treacherously and keep silent when the wicked swallows up the man who is more righteous than he,
units.rightText: Thou that art of purer eyes than to behold evil, and that canst not look on perverseness, wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy peace when the wicked swalloweth up the man that is more righteous than he;

units.leftText: and make men like the fish of the sea, like the creeping things that have no ruler over them?
units.rightText: and makest men as the fishes of the sea, as the creeping things, that have no ruler over them?

units.leftText: He takes up all of them with the hook. He catches them in his net and gathers them in his dragnet. Therefore he rejoices and is glad.
units.rightText: He taketh up all of them with the angle, he catcheth them in his net, and gathereth them in his drag: therefore he rejoiceth and is glad.

units.leftText: Therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, because by them his life is luxurious and his food is good.
units.rightText: Therefore he sacrificeth unto his net, and burneth incense unto his drag; because by them his portion is fat, and his food plenteous.

units.leftText: Will he therefore continually empty his net, and kill the nations without mercy?
units.rightText: Shall he therefore empty his net, and spare not to slay the nations continually?

units.leftText: I will stand at my watch and set myself on the ramparts, and will look out to see what he will say to me, and what I will answer concerning my complaint.
units.rightText: I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will look forth to see what he will speak with me, and what I shall answer concerning my complaint.

units.leftText: The LORD answered me, “Write the vision, and make it plain on tablets, that he who runs may read it.
units.rightText: And Jehovah answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tablets, that he may run that readeth it.

units.leftText: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it, because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
units.rightText: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hasteth toward the end, and shall not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not delay.

units.leftText: Behold, his soul is puffed up. It is not upright in him, but the righteous will live by his faith.
units.rightText: Behold, his soul is puffed up, it is not upright in him; but the righteous shall live by his faith.

units.leftText: Yes, moreover, wine is treacherous: an arrogant man who doesn’t stay at home, who enlarges his desire as Sheol; he is like death and can’t be satisfied, but gathers to himself all nations and heaps to himself all peoples.
units.rightText: Yea, moreover, wine is treacherous, a haughty man, that keepeth not at home; who enlargeth his desire as Sheol, and he is as death, and cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all peoples.
leftNotes: 2:5 Sheol is the place of the dead.

units.leftText: Won’t all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, ‘Woe to him who increases that which is not his, and who enriches himself by extortion! How long?’
units.rightText: Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and that ladeth himself with pledges!

units.leftText: Won’t your debtors rise up suddenly, and wake up those who make you tremble, and you will be their victim?
units.rightText: Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee, and thou shalt be for booty unto them?

units.leftText: Because you have plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples will plunder you because of men’s blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city and to all who dwell in it.
units.rightText: Because thou hast plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples shall plunder thee, because of men’s blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city and to all that dwell therein.

units.leftText: Woe to him who gets an evil gain for his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the hand of evil!
units.rightText: Woe to him that getteth an evil gain for his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the hand of evil!

units.leftText: You have devised shame to your house by cutting off many peoples, and have sinned against your soul.
units.rightText: Thou hast devised shame to thy house, by cutting off many peoples, and hast sinned against thy soul.

units.leftText: For the stone will cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the woodwork will answer it.
units.rightText: For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it.

units.leftText: Woe to him who builds a town with blood, and establishes a city by iniquity!
units.rightText: Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and establisheth a city by iniquity!

units.leftText: Behold, isn’t it from the LORD of Armies that the peoples labor for the fire, and the nations weary themselves for vanity?
units.rightText: Behold, is it not of Jehovah of hosts that the peoples labor for the fire, and the nations weary themselves for vanity?

units.leftText: For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the LORD’s glory, as the waters cover the sea.
units.rightText: For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Jehovah, as the waters cover the sea.

units.leftText: “Woe to him who gives his neighbor drink, pouring your inflaming wine until they are drunk, so that you may gaze at their naked bodies!
units.rightText: Woe unto him that giveth his neighbor drink, to thee that addest thy venom, and makest him drunken also, that thou mayest look on their nakedness!

units.leftText: You are filled with shame, and not glory. You will also drink and be exposed! The cup of the LORD’s right hand will come around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory.
units.rightText: Thou art filled with shame, and not glory: drink thou also, and be as one uncircumcised; the cup of Jehovah’s right hand shall come round unto thee, and foul shame shall be upon thy glory.

units.leftText: For the violence done to Lebanon will overwhelm you, and the destruction of the animals will terrify you, because of men’s blood and for the violence done to the land, to every city and to those who dwell in them.
units.rightText: For the violence done to Lebanon shall cover thee, and the destruction of the beasts, which made them afraid; because of men’s blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city and to all that dwell therein.

units.leftText: “What value does the engraved image have, that its maker has engraved it; the molten image, even the teacher of lies, that he who fashions its form trusts in it, to make mute idols?
units.rightText: What profiteth the graven image, that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, even the teacher of lies, that he that fashioneth its form trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?

units.leftText: Woe to him who says to the wood, ‘Awake!’ or to the mute stone, ‘Arise!’ Shall this teach? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all within it.
units.rightText: Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise! Shall this teach? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it.

units.leftText: But the LORD is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him!”
units.rightText: But Jehovah is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him.

units.leftText: A prayer of Habakkuk, the prophet, set to victorious music.
units.rightText: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, set to Shigionoth.

units.leftText: LORD, I have heard of your fame.
units.rightText: O Jehovah, I have heard the report of thee, and am afraid:

units.leftText: God came from Teman,
units.rightText: God came from Teman,

units.leftText: His splendor is like the sunrise.
units.rightText: And his brightness was as the light;

units.leftText: Plague went before him,
units.rightText: Before him went the pestilence,

units.leftText: He stood, and shook the earth.
units.rightText: He stood, and measured the earth;

units.leftText: I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction.
units.rightText: I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction;

units.leftText: Was the LORD displeased with the rivers?
units.rightText: Was Jehovah displeased with the rivers?

units.leftText: You uncovered your bow.
units.rightText: Thy bow was made quite bare;

units.leftText: The mountains saw you, and were afraid.
units.rightText: The mountains saw thee, and were afraid;

units.leftText: The sun and moon stood still in the sky
units.rightText: The sun and moon stood still in their habitation,

units.leftText: You marched through the land in wrath.
units.rightText: Thou didst march through the land in indignation;

units.leftText: You went out for the salvation of your people,
units.rightText: Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people,

units.leftText: You pierced the heads of his warriors with their own spears.
units.rightText: Thou didst pierce with his own staves the head of his warriors:

units.leftText: You trampled the sea with your horses,
units.rightText: Thou didst tread the sea with thy horses,

units.leftText: I heard, and my body trembled.
units.rightText: I heard, and my body trembled,

units.leftText: For even though the fig tree doesn’t flourish,
units.rightText: For though the fig-tree shall not flourish,

units.leftText: yet I will rejoice in the LORD.
units.rightText: Yet I will rejoice in Jehovah,

units.leftText: GOD, the Lord, is my strength.
units.rightText: Jehovah, the Lord, is my strength;
